title: Room and sleep
intro: Furniture, mattress, bedside crib and lighting. For each item: what to check in the shop and which standard should be on the label.

sections.title: Safe sleep rules
sections.tip: This is the foundation. Fit the rest of your purchases around it.

items.name: Always on the back, on a flat, firm surface
Empty cot: no pillow, duvet, soft toys or bumpers
Sleep in the parents' room, ideally for the first 6 months
items.why: Own cot or a bedside crib next to the parents' bed.

items.name: Room temperature 16–20°C
items.why: Overheating is a SIDS risk factor. Check the back of the neck, not the hands.

items.name: No tobacco smoke at home or near the baby
60×120 cm cot with adjustable base height
criteria: Bar spacing 4.5–6.5 cm
No decorative cut-outs or protruding parts
Stable, doesn't wobble when assembled
Child-safe paint and varnish (marked on the label)
Removable bars come in handy around age 2

items.name: Crib or Moses basket
items.why: For the first 3–4 months. No longer safe once the baby starts rolling over.

sections.title: Bedside crib
sections.tip: Closeness without bed-sharing. A tight fit is key.

items.name: Bedside crib with straps fixing it to the parents' bed frame
criteria: Straps or hooks fixing it to the frame, no gap between the mattresses
Height adjustable to the level of the parents' mattress
High side panel on the parents' side for when it isn't attached
Flat base, no tilt
Check the weight and age limit (usually about 6 months or until sitting up)

items.name: Mattress made for this specific bedside crib
items.why: A mattress from another cot leaves gaps at the edges.

items.name: Firm, flat mattress with a perfect fit
criteria: Gap between mattress and cot side no wider than two fingers
Hand test: the dent springs back quickly, your hand doesn't sink in
New, not used by another child
Removable cover washable at 60°C
OEKO-TEX Standard 100 label on the cover
No memory foam — too soft for a baby

items.name: Waterproof protector under the sheet
Dresser with changing top, anchored to the wall
criteria: Anti-tip brackets — a dresser with open drawers tips over easily
Changing surface at 90–100 cm, at the parent's waist height
Changing mat with raised sides
Everything for changing within reach so you never step away from the baby

items.name: Armchair or comfortable feeding spot with back and arm support
Shelves and pictures screwed down and not above the cot
Cot away from windows, radiators and blind cords
items.why: Blind and curtain cords are a strangulation risk. Tie them up high or fit a cord tensioner.

sections.title: Lighting
sections.tip: At night, light should let you change and feed without waking the baby or yourself.

items.name: Warm, dimmable night light (2700 K or lower, ideally amber)
criteria: Dims to a very low level
Warm or amber colour, no blue light
Battery-powered or with a short cable out of the child's reach
Doesn't shine into the eyes of a lying baby

items.name: Diffused main lighting, not a spotlight above the changing table
items.why: When being changed, the baby lies on their back looking straight at the ceiling.

items.name: Blackout curtains or blinds
items.why: Help with daytime naps and summer sleep.

items.name: Star projector or white-noise lamp
items.why: Optional. Keep the noise quiet and away from the baby's head.

items.name: Thermometer with hygrometer
Humidifier
items.why: In the heating season, when humidity drops below 40%.

items.name: Baby monitor
Breathing monitor
items.why: There's no evidence it prevents SIDS. Consider it if a doctor recommends it.
